statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-46394: in BusyBox tar through 1.37.0, an archive can hide file names from a listing by embedding terminal escape sequences in them (busybox bug 16018, https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2025/04/24/3). The fix makes tar and cpio listings replace unprintable bytes with '?' when writing to a terminal (https://lists.busybox.net/pipermail/busybox/2025-April/091461.html). Every DHI busybox package for Alpine 3.23 is built from the source of Alpine's 3.23-stable busybox package at revision 30 (https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/3.23-stable/main/busybox/APKBUILD), whose secfixes list CVE-2025-46394 as fixed in 1.37.0-r27 and which applies that patch. Inspected every busybox-source package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository for x86_64 and aarch64: busybox (1.37.0-r30, 1.37.0_git20260210-r31, 1.37.0_git20260212-r31 and 1.37.0_git20260817-r32, plus 1.37.0_git20260210-r30 on aarch64), busybox-static (the same versions plus 1.37.0_git20260209-r31), busybox-extras, busybox-suid, busybox-binsh, ssl_client and the doc, openrc and ifupdown packages. tar is an applet of /bin/busybox and /bin/busybox.static only; busybox-extras provides network daemons and clients without tar, and ssl_client and bbsuid are helper programs. Listed an archive holding a file whose name contains an escape byte with tar tf and tar tvf, on a terminal, using every published busybox and busybox.static binary: every one prints that byte as '?'. 1.37.0-r30 is the lowest published version, so with this range every published build is on the fixed side.
